# Communication Management System for Mobile Platforms

## Overview

This disclosure describes a technique and system for handling data communications on a movable platform. The system includes several platform-based applications, a communications framework capable of sending data from these applications through a chosen link from multiple available communication channels, and a module dedicated to managing this data flow.

## Core Functionality

The system and its corresponding method operate through the following process:

**Bandwidth Monitoring**: The system gathers performance metrics reflecting the current available capacity of each communication channel that has been assigned to or is linked with the various platform applications.

**Data Assessment**: For every application running on the platform, the system determines what data needs to be sent to a destination node. It then evaluates the bandwidth needs of this outgoing data against the actual available capacity of the communication link designated for that particular application.

**Insufficiency Detection and Notification**: When this evaluation reveals that a communication link cannot adequately support the bandwidth demands of a particular application's data, the system creates notification information and sends it to that application—or to a quality-of-service interface connected to it.

**Adaptive Response**: Upon receiving this notification, the affected application (or its associated quality-of-service interface) adjusts one or more characteristics of its outgoing data to match the actual bandwidth available on its assigned communication channel, ensuring successful transmission to the intended recipient node.

## Key Benefit

This approach allows individual applications to dynamically modify their data transmission parameters in real-time, responding directly to fluctuations in available network capacity rather than transmitting data that may fail or degrade due to insufficient bandwidth.

# Communications Management System for Moving Platforms

## System Architecture

The system is designed to manage communications for a moving platform, encompassing an integrated architecture that includes multiple platform applications, a communications system capable of supporting several distinct wireless communication links, and a dedicated data management module. This architecture enables the platform to maintain reliable data transmission across varying network conditions that are characteristic of mobile operations.

## Bandwidth Monitoring and Performance Data Collection

Central to the system's operation is its capacity to receive performance data that indicates the current available bandwidth for each communications link. These links are allocated to, or otherwise associated with, the various platform applications operating within the system. This continuous monitoring ensures that the system maintains an up-to-date understanding of network capacity across all active communication channels, which is essential given the dynamic nature of wireless connectivity on a moving platform.

## Bandwidth Requirement Assessment

For each platform application, the system performs a critical evaluation process: it identifies the specific data that is queued for transmission and subsequently compares the bandwidth requirement of that data against the current available bandwidth of the communications link assigned to that application. This per-application analysis allows the system to make informed, granular decisions rather than applying a uniform policy across all applications, thereby accounting for the unique data transmission needs of each individual application.

## Response to Bandwidth Insufficiency

When the system's comparison reveals that the available bandwidth is insufficient to meet a specific application's transmission needs, it takes proactive corrective action. Specifically, the system generates and transmits information data directed to that particular application, or alternatively, to its associated quality of service (QoS) interface. This notification mechanism serves as the trigger for adaptive behavior within the affected application, ensuring that bandwidth constraints are communicated promptly to the relevant component.

## Adaptive Response and Parameter Adjustment

Upon receipt of this information data, the specified application—or its associated quality of service interface—responds by adapting at least one parameter of its data. This adaptation is performed specifically to align the data's transmission requirements with the current available bandwidth of the assigned communications link. Only after this adjustment has been made does the application proceed to transmit the modified data to its intended recipient node.

## Summary

Through this closed-loop feedback mechanism—spanning performance monitoring, bandwidth comparison, notification, and adaptive parameter adjustment—the system ensures that data transmission remains feasible and efficient despite the fluctuating bandwidth conditions inherent to wireless communication links on a moving platform. This approach optimizes resource utilization while maintaining functional communication between platform applications and their respective recipient nodes.

# Communications Management Method and Apparatus for Moving Platforms with Dynamic Bandwidth-Aware Application Adaptation

## Field of the Invention

This invention relates generally to communications management systems for moving platforms, and more particularly to methods and apparatus for monitoring available bandwidth across multiple wireless communication links and dynamically informing platform applications when their data transmission requirements exceed currently available network capacity, thereby enabling adaptive adjustment of application data parameters to maintain reliable communications despite fluctuating link conditions.

## Background of the Invention

Moving platforms—including aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles, maritime vessels, ground vehicles, and other mobile assets—increasingly rely on multiple simultaneous wireless communication links to maintain connectivity with ground stations, satellites, other platforms, and networked infrastructure. These platforms typically host numerous applications that generate data requiring transmission, including sensor telemetry, video surveillance feeds, voice communications, command and control messages, health and status reporting, and various mission-specific data streams.

A fundamental challenge confronting such systems is the inherently variable and often unpredictable nature of wireless communication link bandwidth. Unlike fixed terrestrial networks, communication links associated with moving platforms are subject to numerous factors that cause bandwidth availability to fluctuate significantly and often rapidly. These factors include:

- Changes in platform position and orientation relative to communication infrastructure
- Atmospheric conditions and environmental interference
- Physical obstructions entering or leaving the signal path
- Competing demands from other users sharing the same spectrum or links
- Link handoffs as the platform transitions between different communication resources
- Degradation due to distance, multipath effects, or signal attenuation
- Intentional or unintentional interference sources

Simultaneously, the various applications operating on the moving platform generate data with differing bandwidth requirements, priorities, and tolerances for latency or data loss. A high-definition video feed, for example, may require substantially more bandwidth than a periodic telemetry report, while a critical command-and-control message may demand guaranteed delivery despite bandwidth constraints that would be acceptable to lose for a routine sensor update.

Conventional approaches to managing this mismatch between fluctuating available bandwidth and application data generation have generally suffered from significant limitations. Many existing systems operate applications without any real-time awareness of actual link conditions, resulting in data queuing, transmission delays, dropped packets, or complete communication failures when available bandwidth falls below what is being demanded by the platform's applications collectively. Other approaches rely on static, pre-configured bandwidth allocations that fail to adapt to the dynamic nature of the operating environment, leading to inefficient use of available communication resources during periods of favorable link conditions and communication failures during periods of degraded conditions.

Furthermore, existing systems often lack a mechanism by which individual applications can be made aware of the specific bandwidth constraints they are experiencing, thereby preventing those applications from taking corrective action such as reducing data resolution, adjusting compression parameters, modifying update rates, or otherwise adapting their data generation behavior to match available communication capacity. This absence of a feedback mechanism between the communication management layer and the application layer represents a significant deficiency in prior art systems, resulting in inefficient bandwidth utilization, unnecessary data loss, and degraded overall system performance.

There exists, therefore, a need for an improved communications management method and apparatus that can continuously monitor available bandwidth across multiple wireless communication links associated with a moving platform, compare this available bandwidth against the actual bandwidth requirements of data being generated by platform applications, and provide timely, actionable information back to those applications so that they may dynamically adjust their data generation parameters in response to changing link conditions.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses the foregoing needs by providing a communications management method and apparatus for a moving platform that monitors, in real time, the available bandwidth across a plurality of wireless communication links associated with the platform, and compares this available bandwidth against the bandwidth requirements associated with data generated by one or more applications operating on the platform.

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, the apparatus includes a bandwidth monitoring component configured to determine, on a substantially continuous or periodic basis, the amount of bandwidth currently available across each of the plurality of wireless communication links utilized by the moving platform. This determination may take into account factors such as signal strength, link quality metrics, current utilization by other data streams, protocol overhead, and any other factors affecting the effective throughput available for data transmission.

The apparatus further includes a bandwidth requirement determination component configured to ascertain the bandwidth requirements associated with data being generated, or scheduled to be generated, by one or more applications operating on the moving platform. This may include analyzing data generation rates, packet sizes, required transmission intervals, priority levels, and quality of service requirements associated with each application's data.

A comparison component within the apparatus is configured to compare the available bandwidth, as determined by the bandwidth monitoring component, against the bandwidth requirements, as determined by the bandwidth requirement determination component, for a given application or set of applications. When this comparison reveals that the available bandwidth is insufficient to accommodate the bandwidth requirements of a particular application's data transmission needs, the apparatus generates information data reflective of this insufficiency.

This information data is subsequently sent to the application in question, or alternatively to a quality of service interface associated with that application, so as to prompt the application to dynamically adapt one or more of its data parameters. Such adaptation may include, without limitation, reducing data resolution, altering compression ratios, adjusting frame rates, modifying transmission intervals, prioritizing certain data elements over others, aggregating data prior to transmission, or otherwise altering the manner in which the application generates or formats its data for transmission.

By providing this feedback loop between the communications management apparatus and the platform's applications, the present invention enables applications to autonomously and dynamically respond to changing bandwidth conditions, thereby optimizing overall communication efficiency and helping to ensure reliable data transmission despite the fluctuating nature of wireless communication links associated with a moving platform.

In various embodiments, the invention may be implemented across a wide range of moving platforms, including but not limited to manned and unmanned aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, maritime vessels, submarines, ground vehicles, and other mobile assets that rely on wireless communication links for data transmission. The plurality of wireless communication links monitored by the apparatus may include, without limitation, satellite communication links, line-of-sight radio frequency links, cellular data links, mesh network links, or any combination thereof.

## Detailed Description of Exemplary Embodiments

### System Architecture

Referring generally to the invention, a moving platform in accordance with one exemplary embodiment includes an onboard communications management system comprising several interoperating components. These components may be implemented in hardware, software, firmware, or any combination thereof, and may reside on a single processing unit or be distributed across multiple processing units within the platform's onboard systems architecture.

The communications management system includes a bandwidth monitor, which interfaces with the physical and link-layer components associated with each of the plurality of wireless communication links utilized by the platform. The bandwidth monitor is configured to continuously or periodically sample link conditions and derive an estimate of currently available bandwidth for each respective link. This estimate may be derived using a variety of techniques known to those skilled in the art, including but not limited to signal-to-noise ratio measurements, throughput testing, acknowledgment latency analysis, packet loss rate monitoring, and modem or radio status reporting.

The communications management system further includes an application interface layer, through which the various applications operating on the moving platform communicate their data transmission needs to the communications management system. This application interface layer may take the form of an application programming interface (API), a middleware layer, or a dedicated quality of service (QoS) interface associated with each application or class of applications.

### Bandwidth Monitoring and Comparison Process

In operation, the bandwidth monitor continuously assesses the available bandwidth across each of the plurality of wireless communication links. This assessed bandwidth information is provided to a comparison engine within the communications management system.

Simultaneously, each application operating on the moving platform, either directly or through its associated quality of service interface, communicates its bandwidth requirements to the communications management system. These bandwidth requirements may be expressed in terms of a minimum required bandwidth, a preferred bandwidth, a range of acceptable bandwidth, or any other suitable metric reflective of the application's data transmission needs.

The comparison engine evaluates the available bandwidth against the communicated bandwidth requirements for each application, taking into account any relevant priority levels, quality of service classifications, or other factors that may influence the allocation of available bandwidth among multiple competing applications. Where the available bandwidth is determined to be sufficient to accommodate a given application's requirements, no corrective action is necessarily taken, and the application's data is transmitted according to its existing parameters.

However, where the comparison engine determines that the available bandwidth is insufficient to accommodate a particular application's bandwidth requirements, the communications management system generates information data reflective of this shortfall. This information data may specify, for example, the magnitude of the bandwidth deficit, the specific link or links affected, an estimated duration of the bandwidth shortfall, or a suggested adjustment to the application's data parameters that would bring its requirements into alignment with currently available bandwidth.

### Dynamic Application Adaptation

The generated information data is transmitted to the affected application, or to its associated quality of service interface, via the application interface layer. Upon receipt of this information data, the application (or its QoS interface) is prompted to dynamically adapt one or more of its data parameters in order to reduce its bandwidth requirements to a level compatible with the currently available bandwidth.

Depending on the nature of the application and the type of data being generated, this adaptation may take various forms. For example, a video streaming application may respond by reducing its frame rate, lowering its resolution, or increasing its compression ratio. A sensor data application may respond by reducing its sampling rate, aggregating multiple readings prior to transmission, or transmitting only data that exceeds a specified threshold of significance. A file transfer application may respond by pausing or throttling its transmission rate, or by prioritizing the transmission of certain data segments over others.

In some embodiments, the communications management system may additionally take into account the relative priority of multiple applications competing for available bandwidth, and may generate differentiated information data for each application reflective of its relative priority. For instance, a lower-priority application may be instructed to reduce its bandwidth consumption to a greater degree than a higher-priority application, in order to preserve available bandwidth for more critical data transmission needs.

### Continuous Monitoring and Feedback

The processes of bandwidth monitoring, comparison, and application notification are preferably performed on a continuous or repeated basis throughout operation of the moving platform, such that the communications management system is able to respond dynamically to changing link conditions as they occur. As available bandwidth increases—for example, as the platform moves into a region of improved signal coverage or as competing demands on the communication links decrease—the communications management system may likewise generate information data indicating that an application may increase its data parameters, such as by increasing resolution, sampling rate, or transmission frequency, so as to make fuller use of the available communication resources.

This continuous feedback loop between the communications management system and the platform's applications enables the overall system to dynamically balance the competing demands of multiple applications against the fluctuating availability of communication bandwidth, thereby optimizing the use of available resources and enhancing the reliability and efficiency of data transmission from the moving platform.

### Alternative Embodiments

It will be appreciated by those skilled in the art that the specific techniques used for bandwidth monitoring, bandwidth requirement determination, and information data generation may vary according to the specific implementation and the nature of the moving platform and its associated applications. # Methods and Their Importance in Problem-Solving

A method is a systematic, structured approach used to accomplish a particular task or solve a specific problem. Methods provide a framework that guides individuals through a series of steps, ensuring consistency, efficiency, and reliability in achieving desired outcomes. Whether in scientific research, business operations, education, or everyday life, methods serve as essential tools for organizing thoughts and actions in a logical sequence.

## The Nature of a Method

At its core, a method is more than just a random collection of actions—it is a deliberate, repeatable process designed with a specific goal in mind. A good method typically includes:

1. **Clear objectives** - understanding what needs to be achieved
2. **Defined steps** - a logical sequence of actions to follow
3. **Measurable outcomes** - ways to evaluate success
4. **Adaptability** - the ability to adjust when circumstances change

## Why Methods Matter

The value of having a proper method cannot be overstated. Without a structured approach, tasks can become chaotic, inefficient, and prone to errors. Methods offer several key benefits:

**Consistency**: When a method is followed correctly, it produces similar results each time, which is crucial in fields like manufacturing, scientific experimentation, and quality control.

**Efficiency**: A well-designed method eliminates unnecessary steps and reduces wasted time and resources, allowing people to accomplish more with less effort.

**Reproducibility**: In scientific and academic contexts, having a documented method allows other researchers to replicate studies and verify results, which is fundamental to the advancement of knowledge.

**Problem-solving clarity**: Breaking down complex problems into methodical steps makes them more manageable and less overwhelming.

## Types of Methods

Methods vary widely depending on their application:

- **Scientific methods** involve observation, hypothesis formation, experimentation, and analysis
- **Teaching methods** encompass various pedagogical approaches like lectures, discussions, and hands-on learning
- **Business methods** include strategic planning, project management frameworks, and operational procedures
- **Research methods** cover qualitative and quantitative approaches to gathering and analyzing data

## Conclusion

Ultimately, a method serves as a roadmap that transforms abstract goals into achievable results. By providing structure and direction, methods empower individuals and organizations to tackle challenges more effectively, learn from their processes, and continuously improve their approaches over time. Whether developing a new method or refining an existing one, the goal remains the same: to create a reliable pathway from problem to solution.

# Patent Claim Draft

## Title
**Method and Apparatus for Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation Across Multiple Communication Links on a Mobile Platform with Application Feedback Signaling**

---

### Claim 1 (Independent Method Claim)

A method for managing bandwidth allocation across multiple communication links on a mobile platform, the method comprising:

(a) establishing, by a bandwidth management module executing on the mobile platform, two or more concurrently active communication links, each link having a distinct physical or logical transport medium selected from a group comprising cellular data links, satellite links, Wi-Fi links, and mesh network links;

(b) monitoring, in real time, one or more link-quality parameters for each of the two or more communication links, the link-quality parameters comprising at least available throughput, latency, jitter, and packet error rate;

(c) receiving, from each of a plurality of applications executing on the mobile platform, a bandwidth request specifying a requested data rate and a priority classification associated with data traffic generated by the respective application;

(d) aggregating the bandwidth requests received from the plurality of applications to determine a total requested bandwidth;

(e) comparing the total requested bandwidth against an available aggregate bandwidth derived from the monitored link-quality parameters across the two or more communication links;

(f) allocating, by the bandwidth management module, a portion of the available aggregate bandwidth to each of the plurality of applications based on the priority classification and the comparing step, wherein the allocating comprises dynamically assigning traffic from a given application to one or more of the two or more communication links according to a load-balancing or failover policy;

(g) determining, responsive to the comparing step, that the available aggregate bandwidth is insufficient to satisfy the total requested bandwidth for at least one application of the plurality of applications; and

(h) generating and transmitting, to the at least one application determined to have insufficient allocated bandwidth, a feedback signal indicating a bandwidth-insufficiency condition, the feedback signal comprising at least one of: (i) a quantitative indication of an allocated data rate relative to the requested data rate, (ii) a recommended reduced data rate, or (iii) a notification enabling the at least one application to adjust a data transmission behavior in response thereto.

---

### Claim 2 (Dependent)
The method of claim 1, wherein the feedback signal is transmitted via an application programming interface (API) exposed by the bandwidth management module, and further comprising receiving, from the at least one application, an acknowledgment or a modified bandwidth request generated in response to the feedback signal.

### Claim 3 (Dependent)
The method of claim 1, further comprising re-allocating bandwidth among the plurality of applications in response to a change in the monitored link-quality parameters or in response to a modified bandwidth request received from the at least one application.

### Claim 4 (Dependent)
The method of claim 1, wherein the priority classification is determined based on at least one of: an application type, a user-defined setting, a quality-of-service (QoS) policy, or a mission-critical designation associated with the mobile platform.

### Claim 5 (Dependent)
The method of claim 1, wherein the mobile platform is one of an unmanned aerial vehicle, a ground vehicle, a maritime vessel, or a wearable device, and wherein the two or more communication links comprise at least one link having intermittent connectivity.

### Claim 6 (Dependent)
The method of claim 1, wherein the allocating step further comprises reserving a minimum guaranteed bandwidth for a subset of the plurality of applications designated as high-priority, independent of the bandwidth-insufficiency condition affecting lower-priority applications.

---

### Claim 7 (Independent Apparatus Claim)

An apparatus for managing bandwidth allocation across multiple communication links on a mobile platform, the apparatus comprising:

a plurality of communication interfaces, each configured to establish a communication link over a distinct transport medium;

a link monitoring module configured to measure, in real time, link-quality parameters for each communication link established via the plurality of communication interfaces;

a request-processing module configured to receive bandwidth requests and associated priority classifications from a plurality of applications executing on the mobile platform;

a bandwidth allocation module, communicatively coupled to the link monitoring module and the request-processing module, configured to:

  allocate available aggregate bandwidth, derived from the measured link-quality parameters, among the plurality of applications based on the priority classifications and the bandwidth requests; and

  dynamically distribute application traffic across the plurality of communication interfaces according to a load-balancing or failover policy; and

a feedback generation module configured to detect a bandwidth-insufficiency condition for at least one application and to transmit, to the at least one application, a feedback signal indicating the bandwidth-insufficiency condition and enabling the at least one application to adjust its data transmission behavior.

### Claim 8 (Dependent)
The apparatus of claim 7, wherein the plurality of communication interfaces comprises at least a cellular modem, a satellite transceiver, and a wireless local area network transceiver.

### Claim 9 (Dependent)
The apparatus of claim 7, further comprising a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of the apparatus, cause the apparatus to perform the method of claim 1.

---

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION

**SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR DYNAMIC BANDWIDTH-AWARE DATA RATE ADAPTATION IN MULTI-LINK WIRELESS COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS FOR MOBILE PLATFORMS**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to wireless communication systems for mobile platforms, and more particularly to systems and methods for monitoring available bandwidth across a plurality of heterogeneous wireless communication links and dynamically instructing one or more data-generating applications executing on or in communication with the mobile platform to adjust their data output rate, resolution, compression level, or transmission priority in response to changing network conditions.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Mobile platforms, including but not limited to unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), manned aircraft, watercraft, ground vehicles, satellites, and other autonomous or semi-autonomous conveyances, increasingly rely on wireless communication links to transmit sensor data, telemetry, video streams, and other data-intensive payloads to one or more ground stations, relay nodes, or other receiving entities.

[0003] Such mobile platforms frequently employ multiple, disparate wireless communication technologies simultaneously or interchangeably, including without limitation cellular networks (e.g., 3G, 4G LTE, 5G), satellite communication links, radio frequency (RF) datalinks, microwave links, mesh networking protocols, and Wi-Fi connections. Each such link is characterized by distinct and often time-varying performance characteristics, including available bandwidth, latency, packet loss rate, signal-to-noise ratio, and susceptibility to interference or obstruction.

[0004] Due to the mobility of the platform, environmental factors such as terrain, atmospheric conditions, distance from ground infrastructure, physical obstructions, electromagnetic interference, and network congestion, the available bandwidth on any given wireless link may fluctuate rapidly and unpredictably. Conventional systems typically configure data-generating applications—such as video encoders, sensor payload managers, or telemetry systems—to operate at fixed or manually configured data rates without regard to real-time link conditions.

[0005] This conventional approach suffers from significant deficiencies. When available bandwidth decreases below the data rate demanded by one or more applications, data packets may be dropped, queued indefinitely, or transmitted with unacceptable latency, resulting in degraded data quality, loss of critical information, or communication failure. Conversely, when available bandwidth exceeds current application demand, the excess capacity remains unutilized, representing an inefficient use of available network resources.

[0006] Existing bandwidth management solutions are generally directed to fixed-infrastructure networks and fail to account for the unique challenges presented by mobile platforms traversing dynamic environments with multiple, simultaneously available, heterogeneous wireless links of varying and independently fluctuating capacity. Furthermore, existing solutions generally lack the capability to differentiate among multiple concurrently executing applications based on priority, data type, or mission-criticality when allocating constrained bandwidth resources.

[0007] There exists, therefore, a need for a system and method capable of continuously monitoring available bandwidth across a plurality of wireless links associated with a mobile platform, and dynamically and automatically instructing one or more applications to adjust their data output characteristics in real time so as to optimize the utilization of available bandwidth while preserving the integrity and priority of critical data.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0008] The present invention addresses the foregoing needs by providing a system and method for dynamically managing data output from one or more applications executing on, or associated with, a moving platform based upon real-time monitoring of available bandwidth across a plurality of wireless communication links.

[0009] In one aspect, the invention comprises a bandwidth monitoring module configured to determine, on a substantially continuous or periodic basis, one or more bandwidth metrics associated with each of a plurality of wireless communication links accessible to the moving platform. Such bandwidth metrics may include, without limitation, available throughput, signal quality, latency, packet loss, jitter, and predicted future bandwidth based on historical trends, platform trajectory, or known environmental characteristics.

[0010] In another aspect, the invention comprises a link management module configured to aggregate the bandwidth metrics obtained from the plurality of wireless links and to determine an aggregate available bandwidth, as well as to select, prioritize, or allocate among the plurality of links for the transmission of data from one or more applications.

[0011] In a further aspect, the invention comprises an adaptation control module configured to generate and transmit, to one or more applications executing locally on the moving platform or remotely in communication therewith, one or more control instructions directing said applications to adjust at least one data output parameter. Such data output parameters may include, without limitation, data rate, video resolution, frame rate, compression ratio, sampling rate, packetization scheme, transmission priority, or selective suppression of non-critical data streams.

[0012] In yet a further aspect, the adaptation control module is configured to determine the control instructions based on a comparison between the aggregate available bandwidth (or per-link available bandwidth) and the current or requested data output rate of each application, optionally weighted according to a predetermined or dynamically assigned priority level associated with each application or data type.

[0013] The invention further contemplates embodiments in which the bandwidth monitoring module predicts future bandwidth availability based on the platform's planned or projected trajectory, historical bandwidth data associated with specific geographic locations, known infrastructure limitations, or other predictive factors, thereby enabling proactive, rather than solely reactive, adjustment of application data output.

[0014] The invention still further contemplates embodiments wherein the adaptation control module implements a hierarchical or rule-based prioritization scheme such that, under conditions of constrained bandwidth, data output from lower-priority applications is reduced, delayed, or suspended in preference to preserving the data output of higher-priority applications.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0015] **FIG. 1** illustrates a block diagram of an exemplary mobile platform equipped with a bandwidth-aware data rate adaptation system in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention.

[0016] **FIG. 2** illustrates a functional block diagram depicting the bandwidth monitoring module, link management module, and adaptation control module in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention.

[0017] **FIG. 3** illustrates a flowchart depicting an exemplary method for monitoring bandwidth and dynamically adjusting application data output in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention.

[0018] **FIG. 4** illustrates an exemplary embodiment in which the mobile platform comprises an unmanned aerial vehicle communicating via a plurality of wireless links with a ground control station.

[0019] **FIG. 5** illustrates an exemplary priority-based allocation scheme for distributing constrained bandwidth among a plurality of applications in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

[0020] While the present invention may be embodied in many different forms, several specific embodiments are discussed herein with the understanding that the present disclosure is to be considered only as an example of the principles of the invention and is not intended to limit the invention to the embodiments illustrated.

### I. System Architecture

[0021] Referring to FIG. 1, there is shown a mobile platform 100, which may comprise, without limitation, an unmanned aerial vehicle, a manned aircraft, a ground vehicle, a marine vessel, a satellite, or any other conveyance capable of movement relative to one or more fixed or mobile receiving stations. The mobile platform 100 comprises one or more data-generating applications 110a-110n, a bandwidth monitoring module 120, a link management module 130, an adaptation control module 140, and a plurality of wireless communication interfaces 150a-150n, each configured to establish and maintain a wireless communication link 160a-160n with one or more remote receiving entities 170.

[0022] The data-generating applications 110a-110n may include, without limitation, video capture and encoding applications, sensor data acquisition systems (e.g., LIDAR, radar, infrared, multispectral imaging), telemetry systems, voice communication applications, and file transfer applications. Each application 110a-110n is configured to generate data for transmission via one or more of the wireless communication links 160a-160n and is further configured to receive control instructions from the adaptation control module 140 and to adjust at least one data output parameter in response thereto.

[0023] The plurality of wireless communication interfaces 150a-150n may implement any combination of wireless communication technologies, including without limitation cellular (3G/4G/5G), satellite communication, RF datalink, microwave, mesh networking, Wi-Fi, or any other suitable wireless protocol, and may operate independently, concurrently, or in a coordinated multi-link configuration such as link aggregation or bonding.

### II. Bandwidth Monitoring Module

[0024] The bandwidth monitoring module 120 is configured to continuously or periodically determine one or more bandwidth metrics for each wireless communication link 160a-160n. In certain embodiments, the bandwidth monitoring module 120 determines such metrics by actively probing the link (e.g., via test packet transmission and round-trip time measurement), passively observing actual data throughput and packet loss during normal operation, querying signal strength and quality indicators reported by the wireless communication interface hardware, or a combination thereof.

# COMMUNICATIONS MANAGEMENT APPARATUS FOR MOBILE PLATFORMS WITH MULTIPLE WIRELESS LINKS

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to communications systems for mobile platforms, and more particularly to an apparatus and method for managing multiple wireless communication links on a mobile platform, monitoring bandwidth performance across such links, and dynamically notifying applications to adjust operational parameters in response to bandwidth constraints.

## BACKGROUND

Mobile platforms, including but not limited to aircraft, marine vessels, ground vehicles, and other transportable systems, increasingly rely on multiple simultaneous wireless communication links to maintain connectivity with ground stations, satellites, other mobile platforms, and terrestrial networks. These links may include, without limitation, satellite communication (SATCOM) links, cellular links (e.g., 4G/LTE, 5G), Wi-Fi links, air-to-ground (ATG) links, mesh network links, and other radio frequency links.

A persistent challenge in such environments is that available bandwidth across these links varies significantly and unpredictably due to factors such as platform position, atmospheric conditions, link congestion, handovers between coverage cells, interference, and hardware limitations. Applications executing on or in communication with the mobile platform—such as video streaming applications, telemetry applications, file transfer applications, voice-over-IP applications, and sensor data applications—often are not aware of real-time bandwidth conditions and therefore cannot adapt their data consumption patterns accordingly. This can result in dropped connections, degraded quality of service, buffering, data loss, or inefficient use of available bandwidth.

Existing solutions typically address bandwidth management at the network layer without providing application-level awareness or actionable feedback. There remains a need for a communications management apparatus that can monitor multiple wireless links in real time, aggregate bandwidth performance data across those links, and proactively notify applications so that the applications themselves can adjust their operating parameters to accommodate changing bandwidth conditions.

## SUMMARY

In accordance with one aspect of the present disclosure, a communications management apparatus for a mobile platform is provided. The apparatus generally includes a plurality of wireless communication interfaces, each configured to establish and maintain a wireless link of a different type; a link monitoring module configured to collect bandwidth performance data associated with each of the wireless links; a bandwidth management module configured to analyze the bandwidth performance data and determine whether a bandwidth constraint condition exists with respect to one or more of the wireless links; and a notification module configured to generate and transmit, to one or more applications executing on or in communication with the mobile platform, a notification indicating the bandwidth constraint condition and one or more suggested or required parameter adjustments.

In some embodiments, the bandwidth management module is further configured to select, based on the bandwidth performance data, a preferred wireless link among the plurality of wireless links for routing data traffic associated with a particular application, and to dynamically reassign data traffic among the plurality of wireless links responsive to changing bandwidth conditions.

In some embodiments, the apparatus further includes a policy engine configured to store and apply one or more bandwidth allocation policies, wherein the bandwidth management module determines the bandwidth constraint condition and the notification module generates the notification based at least in part on the one or more bandwidth allocation policies.

Additional aspects, features, and advantages will be apparent from the following detailed description.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** illustrates a block diagram of a mobile platform equipped with a communications management apparatus in accordance with an exemplary embodiment.

**FIG. 2** illustrates a functional block diagram of the communications management apparatus of FIG. 1.

**FIG. 3** illustrates a flow diagram of a method for monitoring bandwidth performance data and notifying applications of bandwidth constraints.

**FIG. 4** illustrates a data structure for bandwidth performance data collected across multiple wireless links.

**FIG. 5** illustrates a sequence diagram showing interaction between the communications management apparatus, a wireless link, and an application during a bandwidth-constrained event.

**FIG. 6** illustrates a block diagram of a computing system suitable for implementing the communications management apparatus.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### I. Overview

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals refer to like elements throughout the several views, FIG. 1 illustrates a mobile platform 100, which in exemplary embodiments may comprise an aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicle, marine vessel, ground vehicle, or other transportable platform. Mobile platform 100 includes a communications management apparatus 110 (also referred to herein as "apparatus 110") communicatively coupled to a plurality of wireless communication interfaces 120a-120n, one or more onboard applications 130a-130n, and, optionally, one or more sensor systems 140.

Each of the wireless communication interfaces 120a-120n is configured to establish and maintain a wireless link of a respective type, such as, without limitation: a satellite communication link, a cellular link (e.g., 4G/LTE, 5G, or successor technologies), a Wi-Fi link, an air-to-ground link, a mesh network link, or any other radio frequency communication link now known or later developed. It will be appreciated that the number and type of wireless communication interfaces 120a-120n may vary according to the requirements of a particular implementation, and that the apparatus 110 is not limited to any particular combination of link types.

### II. Communications Management Apparatus Architecture

Turning to FIG. 2, apparatus 110 is shown in greater detail, comprising a link monitoring module 210, a bandwidth management module 220, a notification module 230, a policy engine 240, a data store 250, and a processing unit 260 configured to execute instructions stored in a memory 270 to carry out the functions of modules 210, 220, 230, and 240. While modules 210-240 are illustrated as discrete functional blocks for purposes of explanation, it will be understood that in various embodiments, the functions attributed to any given module may be combined, distributed, or reorganized among fewer or additional modules, and may be implemented in hardware, software, firmware, or any combination thereof, without departing from the scope of the present disclosure.

**A. Link Monitoring Module**

Link monitoring module 210 is configured to continuously or periodically collect bandwidth performance data 212 associated with each of the wireless links established via wireless communication interfaces 120a-120n. In exemplary embodiments, bandwidth performance data 212 may include, without limitation: (i) available bandwidth (e.g., in bits per second) for a given link at a given time; (ii) latency or round-trip time associated with a given link; (iii) packet loss rate; (iv) jitter; (v) signal strength or signal-to-noise ratio; (vi) link utilization percentage; (vii) historical bandwidth trends over a configurable time window; and (viii) predicted future bandwidth availability based on platform position, trajectory, and known coverage maps.

In some embodiments, link monitoring module 210 obtains bandwidth performance data 212 by querying modem or radio hardware associated with each wireless communication interface 120a-120n directly, for example via a hardware abstraction layer or driver-level application programming interface (API). In other embodiments, link monitoring module 210 obtains bandwidth performance data 212 by performing active probing (e.g., transmitting test packets and measuring round-trip characteristics) or by passively observing ongoing data traffic characteristics.

Bandwidth performance data 212 collected by link monitoring module 210 is stored in data store 250, for example in a data structure such as that illustrated in FIG. 4, which associates each wireless link identifier 410 with a timestamp 420, a set of measured performance metrics 430, and, optionally, a predicted performance value 440 derived from historical trends or platform trajectory data.

**B. Bandwidth Management Module**

Bandwidth management module 220 is configured to analyze bandwidth performance data 212, retrieved from data store 250 or received directly from link monitoring module 210, to determine whether a bandwidth constraint condition exists with respect to one or more of the wireless links. In exemplary embodiments, a bandwidth constraint condition may be determined to exist when one or more measured or predicted performance metrics fail to satisfy a threshold criterion defined by policy engine 240, examples of which include, without limitation:

1. available bandwidth for a given link falling below a minimum threshold value;
2. latency for a given link exceeding a maximum threshold value;
3. packet loss rate for a given link exceeding a maximum threshold percentage;
4. an aggregate bandwidth across all active links falling below a value required to support currently executing applications 130a-130n; or
5. a predicted future bandwidth constraint based on platform trajectory (e.g., an aircraft approaching a region of known degraded satellite coverage).

In some embodiments, bandwidth management module 220 is further configured to select a preferred wireless link, from among wireless communication interfaces 120a-120n, for routing data traffic associated with a particular application 130a-130n, based on the bandwidth performance data 212 and one or more application-specific requirements (e.g., minimum bandwidth, maximum latency, priority level) stored in data store 250 or policy engine 240. Bandwidth management module 220 may dynamically reassign such data traffic among the plurality of wireless links responsive to changing bandwidth conditions, for example by shifting a video streaming application's traffic from a degraded cellular link to an available satellite link.

**C. Notification Module**

Notification module 230 is configured to generate a notification 232 upon a determination, by bandwidth management module 220, that a bandwidth constraint condition exists. Notification 232 is transmitted to one or more of applications 130a-130n executing on or in communication with mobile platform 100, and includes information indicating: (i) the nature and severity of the bandwidth constraint condition; (ii) the affected wireless link or links; (iii) one or more suggested or required parameter adjustments for the receiving application; and, optionally, (iv) an estimated duration of the bandwidth constraint condition, if determinable from historical trends or platform trajectory data.

In exemplary embodiments, the suggested or required parameter adjustments may include, without limitation:

- reducing video or audio streaming bitrate or resolution;
- reducing the frequency or size of telemetry data transmissions;
- deferring non-critical file transfers or software updates;
- switching to a lower-fidelity data compression scheme;
- reducing polling frequency for sensor data;
- prioritizing certain categories of data over others; or
- entering a reduced-bandwidth or "degraded mode" of operation defined by the application itself.

In some embodiments, notification module 230 transmits notification 232 via an application programming interface (API) exposed by apparatus 110, such that applications 130a-130n may subscribe to receive notifications 232 in real time. In other embodiments, notification module 230 transmits notification 232 via a publish-subscribe messaging architecture, a shared memory interface, or an inter-process communication mechanism, depending on the particular software environment of mobile platform 100. In still other embodiments, where an application 130a-130n executes remotely from mobile platform 100 (e.g., at a ground station), notification 232 is transmitted over one or more of the wireless links themselves, optionally using a dedicated low-bandwidth control channel reserved for such management traffic so as to ensure delivery even under severe bandwidth constraint conditions.

In some embodiments, notification module 230 additionally generates a follow-up notification when bandwidth management module 220 determines that the bandwidth constraint condition has been resolved or has improved, thereby allowing applications 130a-130n to restore previously reduced parameters.

# INVENTION SUMMARY

## Method for Dynamic Bandwidth Management in Moving Platform Communications Systems

### Claim 1

A method for managing communications data transmission on a moving platform, the method comprising:

identifying, by a communications management system disposed on the moving platform, data designated for transmission by a plurality of applications executing on or in communication with the moving platform;

determining an available bandwidth associated with one or more communication links accessible to the moving platform, wherein the available bandwidth varies based at least in part on a position, trajectory, or environmental condition associated with the moving platform;

comparing the data designated for transmission by the plurality of applications to the available bandwidth of the one or more communication links to determine whether a bandwidth deficit or surplus condition exists;

providing, via a quality of service (QoS) interface, an indication of the available bandwidth to at least one application of the plurality of applications; and

enabling the at least one application, in response to the indication, to adaptively modify one or more transmission parameters associated with the data designated for transmission, so as to conform the data for transmission to the available bandwidth of the one or more communication links.

---

### Claim 2

The method of claim 1, wherein the one or more transmission parameters comprise at least one of: a data compression ratio, a data resolution, a transmission priority, a transmission rate, a data format, or a data payload size.

---

### Claim 3

The method of claim 1, wherein determining the available bandwidth comprises predicting a future available bandwidth based on a predicted future position of the moving platform relative to a communication node providing the one or more communication links.

---

### Claim 4

The method of claim 1, further comprising:

assigning, by the communications management system, a priority level to each application of the plurality of applications; and

allocating the available bandwidth among the plurality of applications based at least in part on the assigned priority levels.

---

### Claim 5

The method of claim 1, wherein the moving platform comprises an aircraft, a spacecraft, a watercraft, or a land vehicle, and wherein the one or more communication links comprise at least one of a satellite communication link, a cellular communication link, or a line-of-sight radio frequency link.

---

### Claim 6

The method of claim 1, further comprising:

monitoring, by the communications management system, changes in the available bandwidth in real time during operation of the moving platform; and

dynamically updating the indication provided via the QoS interface in response to the monitored changes.

---

### Claim 7

The method of claim 1, wherein enabling the at least one application to adaptively modify the one or more transmission parameters comprises transmitting, via the QoS interface, a recommended transmission parameter set to the at least one application, wherein the at least one application selectively adopts the recommended transmission parameter set.

---

### Claim 8

The method of claim 1, further comprising queuing a portion of the data designated for transmission when the available bandwidth is determined to be insufficient to accommodate the data designated for transmission by the plurality of applications.

---

### Claim 9

The method of claim 1, wherein the QoS interface comprises an application programming interface (API) accessible by each of the plurality of applications to query the available bandwidth and to report the one or more transmission parameters.

---

### Claim 10

A communications system for a moving platform, comprising:

one or more processors; and

a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to perform the method of claim 1.

---

*[Additional dependent claims directed to specific bandwidth prediction algorithms, multi-link aggregation, failover between communication links, and encrypted QoS signaling may be appended as needed based on further disclosure.]*
